hook: Denis Yarats is the co-founder and chief technology officer of Perplexity, the AI answer engine he started in 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Johnny Ho and Andy Konwinski. Before that he was a research scientist at Facebook AI Research and completed a PhD at New York University, where his work on agents that learn control from raw pixels produced the DrQ, DrQ-v2 and Proto-RL methods. Earlier in his career he worked as an engineer at Microsoft and Quora.

quick_facts: Lists his current role as co-founder and CTO of Perplexity AI on his Google Scholar profile, which is verified with a perplexity.ai address (retrieved October 2026).
Born in Gomel, Belarus, he studied at the Faculty of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science of Belarusian State University.
Completed a PhD in artificial intelligence at New York University in 2022.
Worked at Microsoft and then at Quora, where he met future Perplexity co-founder Johnny Ho, before becoming a research scientist at Facebook AI Research.
His Google Scholar profile recorded about 11,000 citations as of October 2026.

achievements.title: Deal or No Deal? (2017)
achievements.impact: With Mike Lewis, Yann Dauphin, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra, built a dataset of human negotiations and trained an end-to-end model that learns to bargain through dialogue, improved by planning with dialogue rollouts.

achievements.title: DrQ (2020)
achievements.impact: With Ilya Kostrikov and Rob Fergus, showed that standard image augmentations let model-free agents such as Soft Actor-Critic learn control from pixels without auxiliary losses or pre-training.

achievements.title: Proto-RL and DrQ-v2 (2021)
achievements.impact: Proto-RL, presented at ICML 2021, learns prototype-based image representations while the agent explores, and DrQ-v2 improved data-augmented continuous control from pixels on the DeepMind Control Suite.

achievements.title: Co-founding Perplexity AI (2022)
achievements.impact: Leads technology at the company, which dropped its first text-to-SQL product to focus on general AI search after a prototype built in late 2022 drew a growing audience.

source_basis: This profile was written mainly from the Wikipedia article on Denis Yarats, retrieved 2026-10-22, with dates and current role checked against his Google Scholar and GitHub profiles, the arXiv records of his papers and interview and profile pages on his career.
